query: For high-entropy alloys intended for high-temperature applications, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain their ability to develop and retain a protective oxide layer that provides oxidation resistance? Specify what governs the behaviour and why, a controlled comparison that would reveal it, the observations expected relative to a baseline, the applicable boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 1 at.% Ti and 1 at.% Al to a high-entropy alloy (HEA) composed of FeCoCrNiMo promotes the formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3-rich oxide layer, which acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion and reduces the oxidation rate, resulting in improved oxidation resistance.
generation.intervention: Alloying with 1 at.% Ti and 1 at.% Al to promote oxide layer formation, with further optimization of the Ti and Al contents and processing conditions
generation.conditions: Exposure to 1000°C in air for 100 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3-rich oxide layer
generation.mechanism: The Ti and Al additions facilitate the formation of a stable, slow-growing oxide layer by promoting the segregation of Al to the surface and the formation of a continuous Al2O3 layer, which acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion and reduces the oxidation rate
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxidation resistance compared to the baseline HEA, as evidenced by a reduced oxide layer thickness and weight gain
generation.baseline: High-entropy alloy (HEA) composed of FeCoCrNiMo without Ti and Al additions
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable to high-entropy alloys composed of FeCoCrNiMo with Ti and Al additions, exposed to high-temperature environments (1000°C) in air
generation.uncertainty: The uncertainty lies in the optimization of the Ti and Al contents and processing conditions to achieve the desired oxide layer morphology and composition

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the oxidation resistance of the high-entropy alloy (HEA) composed of FeCoCrNiMo with and without Ti and Al additions, exposed to 1000°C in air for 100 hours
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxide layer thickness and weight gain of the HEA with Ti and Al additions are not significantly reduced compared to the baseline HEA, the hypothesis is falsified
